review_notes: I read the whole target file and its imports. The two theorems in it do not repeat any nontrivial reasoning with each other, because the second only calls the first through simpa. I then searched the LipschitzHilbert tree for uses of `sum_referenceFamily_selected` and for parallel files. I found that Packets/PacketDataReferenceSelectedVariation.lean repeats the same two theorems, with the same statements and the same tactic proofs, for the parallel structure `PacketLatticeData`. The only differences are the namespace and one extra name in the `unfold` call. I confirmed that `PacketLatticeData` (PacketLatticeData.lean:12) and `SourceLabeledLattice` (SourceSlottedLattice.lean:21) are separate structures. Both define `referenceFamily` with the codomain `SourceLabeledLattice`. I did not compare the full field lists of the two structures. I did not check whether a conversion between them already exists, and I could not run Lean. The proposed shared lemma and conversion are therefore a design sketch that has not been compiled. How much it saves depends on whether `PacketLatticeData.physicalMaskedValue` and `selectedPhysicalPrefix` can be shown to agree with their `SourceLabeledLattice` counterparts. The sibling repetition of the `sum_referenceFamily_selected` + `simpa` pattern in the amplitude and residual theorems is shorter and not strong enough to report separately.

findings.problem: These two theorems, with the same statements and the same proofs, are repeated in Packets/PacketDataReferenceSelectedVariation.lean for `PacketLatticeData`. Only the namespace and the `unfold` list differ. The repeated reasoning is the recentering argument: reduce prefix equality to per-stopping-index sums, apply the selected-sum identity to the masked-value function, and rewrite with `referenceFamily_physicalMaskedValue`. The same pattern recurs in the good-bound corollary. A change to the recentering argument, such as the filter predicate or the masked-value definition, must be made in both files. The same copy-and-paste pattern also covers `sum_referenceFamily_selected`, `referenceFamily_physicalMaskedValue` and the packet amplitude and residual lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Prove the recentering argument once and derive the other version from it. One option is a structure-independent lemma. For any `S`, `stop`, and per-index functions `g` and `g'` with `∀ u ∈ S, g' (reindex u) = g u`, it would say that `packetPrefix (fun k => ∑ q ∈ Qset.filter (stop q.1 = k), g' q)` equals `packetPrefix (fun k => ∑ q ∈ S.filter (stop q.1 = k), g q)`. The proof would be `congr 1; funext k`, then `Finset.sum_filter` and the existing `sum_referenceFamily_selected`. A more direct option is a conversion `PacketLatticeData.toSource : SourceLabeledLattice N κ Label Item`, together with a lemma that `P.selectedPhysicalPrefix` agrees with the source version. Then the `PacketLatticeData` theorems become `exact P.toSource.referenceFamily_selectedPhysicalPrefix …`. They would not be copied proofs. The good-bound corollary needs no separate proof once the prefix identity is transferred. The `simpa` there only rewrites with the identity, so it can be stated for one structure and reused.
findings.benefit: One proof of the recentering step replaces two copies of about 40 lines. Maintenance changes to the physical-mask or stopping-prefix definitions are made once. Readers can see that the two files state the same fact and are not independent results.
